questions.q: Under Article 1 of the Constitution, the territory of India comprises which of the following categories? 1️⃣ Territories of the states 2️⃣ Union territories 3️⃣ Territories that may be acquired by the Government of India at any time.
questions.e: According to Article 1, the Indian territory is divided into three specific categories: the territories of the various states, the union territories, and any territories that the Government of India may acquire in the future. Currently, there are 28 states and 8 union territories.

questions.q: With reference to the Indian federal system, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ States are members of the federal system and share a distribution of power with the Centre. 2️⃣ Union territories are under the direct control and administration of the Central government. 3️⃣ The existence of union territories constitutes a departure from federalism in India.
questions.e: States share constitutional powers with the Centre as part of the federal structure. In contrast, union territories are centrally administered, making the relationship unitary in nature, which is a conspicuous departure from the federal principle.

questions.q: Which of the following areas were formerly known as 'scheduled districts' in 1874 during British rule?
questions.e: During British rule, certain areas were first constituted as 'scheduled districts' in 1874. These were later renamed as 'chief commissioners provinces' before becoming Part C and Part D territories after independence.

questions.q: The 7th Constitutional Amendment Act (1956) was significant for which of the following reasons? 1️⃣ It abolished the four-fold classification of states and territories. 2️⃣ It constituted the 'union territories'. 3️⃣ It was passed alongside the States Reorganisation Act.
questions.e: In 1956, the 7th Constitutional Amendment Act and the States Reorganisation Act replaced the previous four-fold classification (Part A, B, C, D) of states and territories with the current system of states and union territories.

questions.q: Which of the following states were formerly union territories before being elevated to statehood? 1️⃣ Himachal Pradesh 2️⃣ Manipur 3️⃣ Mizoram 4️⃣ Goa
questions.e: Several current states were initially union territories. These include Himachal Pradesh, Manipur, Tripura, Mizoram, Arunachal Pradesh, and Goa.

questions.q: Consider the following pairs of Union Territories and their year of creation: 1️⃣ Andaman and Nicobar Islands: 1956 2️⃣ Chandigarh: 1966 3️⃣ Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu: 2020. How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Andaman and Nicobar Islands were created in 1956. Chandigarh was created in 1966. The merger of Dadra and Nagar Haveli with Daman and Diu into a single union territory took place in 2020.

questions.q: Which Union Territory was known as Laccadive, Minicoy and Amindivi Islands until 1973?
questions.e: The name Lakshadweep was adopted in 1973; prior to this, the islands were referred to as the Laccadive, Minicoy, and Amindivi Islands.

questions.q: Delhi was redesignated as the National Capital Territory of Delhi in which year?
questions.e: While the 69th Amendment Act was passed in 1991, Delhi was formally redesignated as the National Capital Territory of Delhi with effect from February 1, 1992.

questions.q: Which of the following Union Territories were created primarily due to 'cultural distinctiveness'? 1️⃣ Puducherry 2️⃣ Dadra and Nagar Haveli 3️⃣ Daman and Diu 4️⃣ Lakshadweep
questions.e: Puducherry (formerly French) and Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu (formerly Portuguese) were created as UTs to preserve their distinct cultural heritage. Lakshadweep was created for strategic importance.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding the creation of the UTs of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh in 2019: 1️⃣ Ladakh was created due to a long-pending demand to realize the aspirations of its people. 2️⃣ The Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir was created keeping in view the internal security situation. 3️⃣ Both new Union territories were provided with a local legislature.
questions.e: While Ladakh and J&K were both created in 2019, only Jammu and Kashmir was provided with a legislature. Ladakh is a union territory without a legislature.

questions.q: What were the reasons provided by the government for the merger of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu in 2020? 1️⃣ Shared administrative set-up, language, and culture. 2️⃣ To reduce duplicacy and wasteful expenditure. 3️⃣ To achieve the policy of "Minimum Government, Maximum Governance".
questions.e: The merger aimed to improve administrative efficiency, use officer services more effectively, and reduce the financial burden caused by parallel departments and secretariats in two small, geographically close territories.

questions.q: Which Articles in Part VIII of the Constitution deal with the administration of Union Territories?
questions.e: Part VIII of the Indian Constitution contains Articles 239, 239A, 239AA, 239AB, 239B, 240, and 241, which govern the administrative framework of all union territories.

questions.q: With reference to the Administrator of a Union Territory, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Every UT is administered by the President acting through an administrator. 2️⃣ The administrator is the constitutional head of the UT, similar to a Governor of a state. 3️⃣ The President can specify the designation of the administrator as Lieutenant Governor or Chief Commissioner.
questions.e: The administrator is an agent of the President, not a constitutional head of state like a Governor. The President has the power to appoint them and define their designation, such as Lt. Governor or Administrator.

questions.q: In which of the following Union Territories is the executive head designated as 'Administrator' rather than 'Lieutenant Governor'? 1️⃣ Chandigarh 2️⃣ Lakshadweep 3️⃣ Puducherry 4️⃣ Delhi
questions.e: Currently, the head is a Lieutenant Governor in Delhi, Puducherry, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, J&K, and Ladakh. In Chandigarh, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, and Lakshadweep, the head is called an Administrator.

questions.q: When the Governor of a state is appointed as the administrator of an adjoining union territory, how do they exercise their functions?
o: In consultation with the Union Home Minister
On the advice of the UT Legislative Assembly
On the advice of the State Council of Ministers
Independently of the State Council of Ministers
questions.e: According to the Constitution, if a Governor is given additional charge of an adjoining UT, they must act independently of their state's council of ministers in their capacity as the UT administrator.

questions.q: Which of the following Union Territories have been provided with a legislative assembly and a council of ministers? 1️⃣ Delhi 2️⃣ Puducherry 3️⃣ Jammu and Kashmir 4️⃣ Ladakh
questions.e: Out of the eight UTs, only three (Delhi, Puducherry, and Jammu and Kashmir) have their own local legislatures and councils of ministers. Ladakh does not have a legislature.

questions.q: Regarding the legislative power of Parliament over Union Territories, which statement is correct?
o: Parliament can only make laws on subjects in the Union List.
Laws made by a UT Assembly prevail over Parliament laws in case of conflict.
Parliament's power to make laws on the State List for UTs remains unaffected even if they have a local legislature.
Parliament cannot make laws on the State List for UTs with a legislature.
questions.e: Parliament has the supreme power to make laws on any subject (Union, State, or Concurrent List) for union territories. This power is not diminished by the creation of a local legislature in UTs like Delhi or Puducherry.

questions.q: The legislative assembly of Delhi can make laws on any subject of the State List except which of the following? 1️⃣ Public Order 2️⃣ Police 3️⃣ Land 4️⃣ Education
questions.e: While Delhi has a legislature, its power is restricted. It cannot legislate on 'Public Order', 'Police', and 'Land'—these subjects remain under the direct control of the Central government.

questions.q: In the case of Puducherry, when can the President legislate by making regulations for its peace, progress, and good government?
o: Only on the advice of the Chief Minister
Only when the assembly is suspended or dissolved
questions.e: The President can make regulations for several UTs (like Lakshadweep or Ladakh) at any time, but for Puducherry, this power can only be exercised if the local assembly is not functioning (suspended or dissolved).

questions.q: A regulation made by the President for a Union Territory has the same force as which of the following?
questions.e: Regulations made by the President under Article 240 have the same force and effect as an Act of Parliament. Such regulations can even repeal or amend an existing Act of Parliament in relation to those UTs.

questions.q: Which is the only Union Territory that has had its own High Court since 1966?
questions.e: Delhi is unique among union territories as it has possessed its own dedicated High Court since 1966. Other UTs are either under the jurisdiction of a neighboring state's High Court or share a common one.

questions.q: Match the following Union Territories with their respective High Court jurisdictions: 1️⃣ Andaman and Nicobar: Calcutta 2️⃣ Lakshadweep: Kerala 3️⃣ Puducherry: Madras 4️⃣ Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu: Bombay. How many pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Most UTs fall under the jurisdiction of adjacent state High Courts. Andaman and Nicobar (Calcutta), Lakshadweep (Kerala), Puducherry (Madras), and Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu (Bombay) are all correctly matched.

questions.q: Under the 69th Constitutional Amendment Act of 1991, what is the fixed strength of the Council of Ministers for Delhi?
questions.e: The Act specifies that the Council of Ministers for Delhi shall consist of not more than ten percent of the total number of members in the Legislative Assembly. Since the assembly has 70 members, the council has 7 ministers.

questions.q: Who appoints the Chief Minister of the National Capital Territory of Delhi?
o: The Chief Justice of Delhi High Court
questions.e: Unlike states where the Governor appoints the CM, in Delhi, the Chief Minister is appointed by the President. Other ministers are also appointed by the President on the advice of the Chief Minister.

questions.q: In the National Capital Territory of Delhi, what happens if there is a difference of opinion between the Lieutenant Governor and his ministers?
o: The matter is referred to the Delhi High Court.
The Lieutenant Governor's decision is final.
The Lt. Governor refers the matter to the President for a decision.
The decision of the Chief Minister is final.
questions.e: In case of a deadlock or disagreement between the Lt. Governor and the Council of Ministers, the Lt. Governor is required to refer the dispute to the President and act according to the President's decision.

questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution provides for the imposition of President's Rule in the Union Territory of Delhi in case of failure of constitutional machinery?
questions.e: While Article 356 applies to states, Article 239AB specifically provides for the suspension of the constitutional provisions in Delhi and the imposition of President's rule.

questions.q: An ordinance promulgated by the Lieutenant Governor of Delhi must be approved by the assembly within how many weeks from its reassembly?
questions.e: Similar to the power of a Governor, an ordinance issued by the Lt. Governor of Delhi during the recess of the assembly has the force of law but must be approved by the assembly within six weeks of its meeting.

questions.q: Which Ministry is the nodal ministry for all matters of Union Territories relating to legislation, finance, and budget?
questions.e: The Ministry of Home Affairs acts as the nodal ministry for all UTs, handling administrative, legislative, and financial matters, including the appointment of Lt. Governors and Administrators.

questions.q: Consider the following regarding the Home Minister's Advisory Committee (HMAC): 1️⃣ It exists for UTs without a legislature. 2️⃣ It is chaired by the Union Home Minister. 3️⃣ Members of Parliament from the UTs are members of this committee.
questions.e: For UTs without legislatures (like Ladakh or Chandigarh), the HMAC provides a forum for discussing social and economic development. It is chaired by the Union Home Minister and includes local MPs and elected members of local bodies.

questions.q: Which of the following statements comparing States and UTs is incorrect?
o: The executive head of a state is the Governor, while for a UT it is an administrator or Lt. Governor.
There is uniformity in the administrative set-up of all UTs.
States have autonomy, while UTs do not.
States have a federal relationship with the Centre, while UTs have a unitary relationship.
questions.e: Unlike states, which have a uniform administrative structure (Governor, CM, Assembly), there is no uniformity in UTs; some have legislatures, some don't, and the designations of their heads vary.

questions.q: Article 244 in Part X of the Constitution envisages a special system of administration for which of the following?
questions.e: Part X of the Constitution, specifically Article 244, provides for a distinct administrative framework for areas designated as 'Scheduled Areas' and 'Tribal Areas' to protect their unique social and cultural interests.

questions.q: The Fifth Schedule of the Constitution deals with the administration of scheduled areas in which of the following states? 1️⃣ Assam 2️⃣ Meghalaya 3️⃣ Jharkhand 4️⃣ Odisha
questions.e: The Fifth Schedule applies to scheduled areas in any state *except* the four North-eastern states of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram, which are instead covered under the Sixth Schedule.

questions.q: Who is empowered to declare an area to be a 'Scheduled Area'?
questions.e: The President of India has the sole authority to declare an area as a Scheduled Area. The President can also alter boundaries or rescind the designation in consultation with the Governor of the concerned state.

questions.q: What are the criteria for declaring an area as a 'Scheduled Area'? 1️⃣ Preponderance of tribal population 2️⃣ Compactness and reasonable size 3️⃣ Economic backwardness 4️⃣ Viable administrative entity like a District or Block
questions.e: Though not explicitly spelt out in the Constitution, these four criteria (tribal population, size, administrative viability, and economic backwardness) have become well-established for such declarations.

questions.q: With reference to the administration of Scheduled Areas, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The executive power of the Centre extends to giving directions to the states regarding these areas. 2️⃣ The Governor must submit an annual report to the President regarding their administration. 3️⃣ The executive power of the state does not extend to scheduled areas.
questions.e: The state's executive power *does* extend to scheduled areas, but the Governor has a special responsibility to report to the President, and the Centre can issue binding directions to the state.

questions.q: How many members constitute the Tribes Advisory Council in a state having scheduled areas?
questions.e: Each state with scheduled areas must establish a Tribes Advisory Council consisting of 20 members. Three-fourths of these members must be representatives of Scheduled Tribes in the state legislative assembly.

questions.q: Who has the power to decide whether an Act of Parliament applies to a Scheduled Area?
questions.e: The Governor is empowered to direct that any particular law of Parliament or the state legislature shall not apply to a scheduled area, or shall apply only with specific modifications.

questions.q: The Sixth Schedule of the Constitution applies to tribal areas in which group of states?
questions.e: The Sixth Schedule provides for autonomous districts and self-rule in the tribal areas of four specific states: Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram.

questions.q: Why does the Sixth Schedule emphasize "self-rule" more than the Fifth Schedule?
o: Because the areas are geographically isolated.
Because the tribes there are more educated.
Because the state governments requested it.
Because many of these communities had ruled themselves until British subjugation.
questions.e: The rationality lies in history; tribal communities in the Sixth Schedule regions maintained significant independence and self-governance until the 19th Century, necessitating a framework that preserves their democratic traditions.

questions.q: Each autonomous district under the Sixth Schedule has a district council consisting of how many members?
questions.e: District councils consist of 30 members. Out of these, 4 are nominated by the Governor (serving at his pleasure), and 26 are elected via adult franchise for a 5-year term.

questions.q: Laws made by district and regional councils on matters like land, forests, and marriage require the assent of whom?
questions.e: While autonomous councils have legislative powers over specific local matters, all laws passed by them must receive the assent of the Governor to become valid.

questions.q: Which body is described as the "watch-dog of merit system" in India?
questions.e: The Constitution visualizes the UPSC as the 'watch-dog of merit system', responsible for conducting examinations for recruitment to All-India and Central services based on merit.

questions.q: What is the term of office for the Chairman and members of the UPSC?
questions.e: UPSC members hold office for a fixed term of six years or until they reach the age of 65, whichever comes earlier. They can resign by addressing the President.

questions.q: On what grounds can the President remove a member of the UPSC without a Supreme Court enquiry? 1️⃣ Adjudged an insolvent 2️⃣ Engages in paid employment outside duties 3️⃣ Infirmity of mind or body 4️⃣ Misbehaviour
questions.e: The President can remove a member directly for insolvency, outside employment, or infirmity. However, for 'misbehaviour', the President *must* refer the matter to the Supreme Court for an enquiry.

questions.q: The expenses of the UPSC, including salaries and pensions, are:
o: Paid by the Ministry of Personnel
Charged on the Contingency Fund of India
Charged on the Consolidated Fund of India
questions.e: To ensure independence, the expenses of the UPSC are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India, meaning they are not subject to the annual vote of Parliament.

questions.q: With reference to the Election Commission, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It is a permanent and independent body. 2️⃣ It conducts elections to Panchayats and Municipalities. 3️⃣ It is common to both the Central and State governments.
questions.e: The Election Commission is an All-India body for Parliament and State Legislature elections. However, it is *not* concerned with local body elections (Panchayats/Municipalities), which are handled by State Election Commissions.

questions.q: Who determines the number of Election Commissioners in the Election Commission?
questions.e: Article 324 states that the Commission shall consist of the Chief Election Commissioner and such number of other commissioners as the President may from time to time fix.

questions.q: Article 280 of the Constitution provides for which quasi-judicial body?
questions.e: Article 280 mandates the President to constitute a Finance Commission every fifth year to recommend the distribution of taxes between the Centre and States.

questions.q: The Finance Commission consists of a chairman and how many other members?
questions.e: The Commission is composed of a chairman (with experience in public affairs) and four other members appointed by the President.

questions.q: Which Constitutional Amendment Act introduced the Goods and Services Tax (GST) Council?
questions.e: The 101st Amendment Act of 2016 inserted Article 279-A, which empowered the President to constitute the GST Council as a joint forum of the Centre and the States.

questions.q: In the GST Council, what is the weightage of the vote of the Central Government?
questions.e: For any decision in the GST Council, the Central Government's vote has a weightage of 1/3rd, while all State Governments combined have a weightage of 2/3rds of the total votes cast.

questions.q: Which Article provides for the National Commission for Scheduled Castes?
questions.e: Article 338 provides for the NCSC. Article 338-A (NCST) and 338-B (NCBC) were added later through constitutional amendments.

questions.q: The National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC) became a constitutional body through which amendment?
questions.e: Originally a statutory body created in 1993, the NCBC was granted constitutional status by the 102nd Amendment Act of 2018, which inserted Article 338-B.

questions.q: Who appoints the chairman and members of the National Commission for SCs?
o: The Union Minister for Social Justice
questions.e: The Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson, and other members of the NCSC are appointed by the President by warrant under his hand and seal.

questions.q: The National Commission for SCs also investigates matters related to which other community?
questions.e: Under Article 338, the NCSC is required to discharge the same functions for the protection and welfare of the Anglo-Indian Community as it does for the Scheduled Castes.

questions.q: The 89th Constitutional Amendment Act of 2003 is famous for:
o: Bifurcating the combined commission for SCs and STs
questions.e: This amendment bifurcated the combined National Commission for SCs and STs into two separate bodies: the NCSC (Art 338) and the NCST (Art 338-A).

questions.q: Which body is responsible for providing the "vision of enhancing active engagement and deepening electoral democracy"?
questions.e: The vision statement of the Election Commission of India focuses on becoming an institution of excellence that strengthens electoral democracy both in India and globally.

questions.q: The Chairman of the UPSC, on ceasing to hold office, is:
o: Eligible for appointment as a Governor
Eligible for appointment as Chief Election Commissioner
Ineligible for further employment under the Government of India or a state
Eligible for a second term in UPSC
questions.e: To maintain independence, the UPSC Chairman is strictly prohibited from any further employment under the Central or State governments after retirement (though the SC has ruled that the office of Governor is not 'employment').

questions.q: A Joint State Public Service Commission (JSPSC) is which type of body?
questions.e: Unlike UPSC and SPSC, a JSPSC is not created directly by the Constitution. It is created by an Act of Parliament following a request from the concerned state legislatures.

questions.q: Which High Court has jurisdiction over the Union Territory of Chandigarh?
questions.e: Chandigarh does not have its own High Court; it falls under the jurisdiction of the common High Court for the states of Punjab and Haryana.

questions.q: Which of the following statements regarding the Lieutenant Governor of Delhi is correct? 1️⃣ He is the constitutional head of the state. 2️⃣ He is empowered to promulgate ordinances during the recess of the assembly. 3️⃣ He can withdraw an ordinance at any time. 4️⃣ He can promulgate an ordinance even when the assembly is dissolved.
questions.e: The Lieutenant Governor is an agent of the President, not a constitutional head. He can issue ordinances during assembly recess and withdraw them at any time, but he cannot do so if the assembly is dissolved or suspended.

questions.q: With reference to the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC), consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The President determines the number of members of the Commission. 2️⃣ One-half of the members must have held office for at least ten years under the Government. 3️⃣ The Constitution prescribes specific educational qualifications for members.
questions.e: The Constitution does not specify the strength of the UPSC, leaving it to the President's discretion. It prescribes no specific qualifications except that half the members must have 10 years of government service experience.

questions.q: Which of the following matters are kept outside the functional jurisdiction of the UPSC? 1️⃣ Making reservations of appointments for any backward class. 2️⃣ Taking into consideration claims of SCs and STs for appointments. 3️⃣ Selection for a temporary appointment lasting less than one year.
questions.e: The UPSC is not consulted on reservations for backward classes or claims of SC/ST groups in appointments. It is also bypassed for temporary appointments expected to last less than a year.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding the State Public Service Commission (SPSC): 1️⃣ Members are appointed by the Governor but removed by the President. 2️⃣ The age of retirement for SPSC members is 65 years. 3️⃣ A member of SPSC is eligible for appointment as Chairman of the same SPSC.
questions.e: SPSC members are appointed by the Governor but can only be removed by the President. Their retirement age is 62 years, not 65 (which applies to UPSC). A member is eligible to become the Chairman of that SPSC.

questions.q: Who acts as the ex-officio Secretary to the Goods and Services Tax (GST) Council?
questions.e: While the Union Finance Minister chairs the GST Council, the Union Revenue Secretary serves as the ex-officio Secretary to the Council.

questions.q: In the case of a failure of constitutional machinery in the National Capital Territory of Delhi, the President can impose rule based on the report of:
questions.e: If the administration of Delhi cannot be carried out according to constitutional provisions, the President can impose his rule based on a report from the Lt. Governor or otherwise.

questions.q: Which body is responsible for the "superintendence, direction and control of elections" to the office of the Vice-President of India?
questions.e: Article 324 vests the power of superintendence, direction, and control of elections to Parliament, state legislatures, the President, and the Vice-President in the Election Commission.

questions.q: With reference to the Sixth Schedule, who is empowered to organize and re-organize the autonomous districts?
questions.e: The Governor of the concerned state has the power to define boundaries, change names, or increase/decrease the areas of autonomous districts in Sixth Schedule states.

questions.q: Which Constitutional Amendment Act bifurcated the combined National Commission for SCs and STs?
questions.e: The 89th Constitutional Amendment Act of 2003 split the combined commission into the National Commission for Scheduled Castes (Article 338) and the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes (Article 338-A).

questions.q: The Chairman and members of the Finance Commission are eligible for:
questions.e: According to Article 280, the chairman and four members of the Finance Commission hold office for the period specified by the President and are eligible for reappointment.

questions.q: What is the quorum required for conducting a meeting of the GST Council?
questions.e: To hold a meeting of the GST Council, a quorum of one-half of the total number of members of the Council is mandatory.

questions.q: The "Mandal case" judgement (1992) is associated with the establishment of which body?
questions.e: In the Indra Sawhney vs. Union of India (1992) case, the Supreme Court directed the government to create a permanent body for backward classes, leading to the NCBC Act of 1993.

questions.q: Which state legislature was exempted from consulting the National Commission for Backward Classes regarding its own list of backward classes in 2021?
questions.e: The 105th Amendment Act of 2021 exempted all state governments from the requirement to consult the NCBC when preparing or maintaining their own lists of socially and educationally backward classes.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding the Finance Commission: 1️⃣ It is a quasi-judicial body. 2️⃣ Its recommendations are binding on the Government of India. 3️⃣ It is constituted by the President every fifth year.
questions.e: The Finance Commission is a quasi-judicial constitutional body constituted every five years. However, its recommendations are advisory and not legally binding on the government.

questions.q: Which of the following is the common High Court for the Union Territories of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh?
o: High Court of J&K and Ladakh
questions.e: The Jammu and Kashmir & Ladakh High Court serves as the common judicial authority for both the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union Territory of Ladakh.

questions.q: The strength of the Legislative Assembly of Jammu and Kashmir as mentioned in the text is:
questions.e: According to the text, the assembly of Puducherry has 30 members, Delhi has 70, and Jammu and Kashmir is provided with 83 members.

questions.q: With reference to the UPSC, the term "misbehaviour" includes which of the following? 1️⃣ Being interested in a contract made by the Government of India. 2️⃣ Participating in the profit of a government agreement. 3️⃣ Being a member of an incorporated company.
questions.e: A member is guilty of misbehaviour if they are interested in a government contract or profit from it, unless they do so as a member of an incorporated company in common with other members.

questions.q: Who chairs the Administrator's Advisory Committee (AAC) in Union Territories without a legislature?
questions.e: While the Home Minister's Advisory Committee (HMAC) is chaired by the Union Home Minister, the AAC is chaired by the Administrator of the specific Union Territory.

questions.q: Under the Sixth Schedule, a District Council can consist of how many nominated members?
questions.e: Of the 30 members in a Sixth Schedule district council, 4 are nominated by the Governor and 26 are elected by the people.

questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution deals with the creation of local legislatures or Council of Ministers for certain Union Territories?
questions.e: Article 239A provides for the creation of local legislatures or councils of ministers for certain union territories, such as Puducherry.

questions.q: The first Finance Commission was headed by:
questions.e: The First Finance Commission was appointed in 1951 and was chaired by K.C. Neogy.

questions.q: The 102nd Amendment Act of 2018 inserted which Article to enable the President to specify socially and educationally backward classes?
questions.e: While Article 338-B established the Commission, Article 342-A was inserted to empower the President to specify the backward classes.

questions.q: Which of the following Union Territories are placed under the jurisdiction of the Calcutta High Court?
questions.e: The text states that Andaman and Nicobar Islands are under the Calcutta High Court, while Lakshadweep is under Kerala and Puducherry is under Madras.

questions.q: How many states currently have Scheduled Areas under the Fifth Schedule?
questions.e: Currently, ten states have scheduled areas: Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Odisha, and Rajasthan.

questions.q: Which of the following is a function of the Election Commission of India at the district level? 1️⃣ The Collector acts as the district returning officer. 2️⃣ The Collector appoints a returning officer for every constituency. 3️⃣ The Collector appoints presiding officers for every polling booth.
questions.e: At the district level, the Collector serves as the district returning officer and is responsible for appointing returning officers for constituencies and presiding officers for polling booths.

questions.q: A member of the UPSC is not eligible for which of the following after ceasing to hold office? 1️⃣ Appointment as Chairman of UPSC. 2️⃣ Appointment as Chairman of an SPSC. 3️⃣ Any other employment under the Government of India.
questions.e: A member of UPSC can be appointed as the Chairman of UPSC or an SPSC, but they are barred from any other government employment.

questions.q: The National Commission for Scheduled Tribes was established in which year as a separate body?
questions.e: Following the 89th Amendment Act of 2003, the separate National Commission for STs formally came into existence in 2004.

questions.q: Which official acts as the "agent of the President" in a Union Territory?
questions.e: Every union territory is administered by the President through an administrator, who acts as the President's agent rather than an independent head of state like a Governor.

questions.q: Under Article 240, the President can make regulations for the peace and good government of which UT? 1️⃣ Ladakh 2️⃣ Lakshadweep 3️⃣ Delhi 4️⃣ Chandigarh
questions.e: The President has regulatory powers for Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Lakshadweep, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, and Ladakh. He does not have this power for Delhi or Chandigarh under this specific Article.

questions.q: In the National Capital Territory of Delhi, the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to:
questions.e: Similar to the cabinet in a state or the Centre, the Council of Ministers in Delhi is collectively responsible to the local Legislative Assembly.

questions.q: Which of the following bodies is described as "a constitution within a constitution"?
questions.e: The Fifth Schedule, which deals with the administration and control of scheduled areas and tribes, has been referred to as "a constitution within a constitution" due to its specialized system.

questions.q: Who determines the qualifications for the members of the Finance Commission?
questions.e: While the President appoints the members, the Constitution authorizes Parliament to determine the qualifications of the members and the manner of their selection.

questions.q: The Secretariat of the GST Council is located in:
questions.e: The GST Council's headquarters/Secretariat is established in New Delhi.

questions.q: Which of the following is correct regarding the removal of the Chairman of an SPSC? 1️⃣ He is appointed by the Governor. 2️⃣ He is removed by the Governor. 3️⃣ He is removed by the President.
questions.e: While the Governor has the power of appointment, the power of removal of an SPSC Chairman rests solely with the President.

questions.q: How many "other members" are there in the National Commission for Scheduled Castes, excluding the Chairperson and Vice-Chairperson?
questions.e: The NCSC consists of a chairperson, a vice-chairperson, and three other members, all appointed by the President.

questions.q: The Sixth Schedule regions are different from Fifth Schedule regions because they emphasize:
questions.e: The Sixth Schedule specifically emphasizes self-rule for tribal communities in the North-East because many of them were self-governing until British rule.

questions.q: Which Article provides for "Special provisions with respect to Delhi"?
questions.e: Article 239AA was inserted to provide the special status and administrative framework for the National Capital Territory of Delhi.

questions.q: The "Annual Report" of the UPSC is presented to whom?
questions.e: The UPSC is constitutionally required to present an annual report on its performance to the President, who then lays it before both Houses of Parliament.

questions.q: With reference to the removal of the Chairman or any other member of the UPSC, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The President can remove them if they are adjudged an insolvent. 2️⃣ The President can remove them if they engage in paid employment outside their office duties. 3️⃣ The advice tendered by the Supreme Court regarding removal for misbehaviour is binding on the President.
questions.e: The President may remove a member for insolvency, infirmity, or outside paid employment. In cases of misbehaviour, the President must refer the matter to the Supreme Court, and its advice is legally binding.

questions.q: Which of the following constitutional articles deals with the power of the President to make regulations for certain Union Territories?
questions.e: Article 240 empowers the President to make regulations for the peace, progress, and good government of specific UTs like Andaman and Nicobar Islands and Lakshadweep. These regulations can even amend or repeal acts of Parliament.

questions.q: The 101st Amendment Act of 2016 is associated with the establishment of which body?
questions.e: The 101st Amendment Act of 2016 introduced the GST regime and provided for the establishment of the GST Council to facilitate consultation between the Centre and the States.

questions.q: Which of the following subjects are excluded from the legislative power of the Assembly of Delhi? 1️⃣ Public Order 2️⃣ Police 3️⃣ Land 4️⃣ Local Government
questions.e: The legislative assembly of Delhi has the power to make laws on subjects in the State List and Concurrent List, except for three specific matters: public order, police, and land.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding the Tribes Advisory Council (TAC): 1️⃣ It must be established in every state having scheduled areas. 2️⃣ It consists of 20 members. 3️⃣ Three-fourths of the members must be representatives of the STs in the state legislative assembly.
questions.e: Each state with scheduled areas is constitutionally required to establish a TAC to advise on the welfare of scheduled tribes. It consists of 20 members, with 75% being ST representatives from the state assembly.

questions.q: Who has the power to appoint an acting chairman for a State Public Service Commission (SPSC)?
o: The Chief Justice of the High Court
questions.e: The Governor of a state is authorized to appoint one of the members of the SPSC as an acting chairman if the office is vacant or if the chairman is unable to perform their duties.

questions.q: The "Vision" of the Election Commission of India includes which of the following?
o: Developing human resources for professional delivery.
Deepening and strengthening electoral democracy globally.
Ensuring the participation of all eligible citizens.
questions.e: The vision of the ECI is to be an institution of excellence by enhancing active engagement and deepening electoral democracy in India and globally. The other options listed are part of its mission or guiding principles.

questions.q: Which High Court has jurisdiction over the Union Territory of Lakshadweep?
questions.e: The Union Territory of Lakshadweep is placed under the jurisdiction of the Kerala High Court.

questions.q: With reference to the Finance Commission, which of the following statements is correct?
o: It is constituted by the President every fifth year.
Members are not eligible for reappointment.
The Chairman must be a judge of the High Court.
questions.e: The Finance Commission is a quasi-judicial body constituted by the President every fifth year or earlier. Members are eligible for reappointment. While a judge can be a member, the chairman should be a person with experience in public affairs.

questions.q: In the context of the Fifth Schedule, who is authorized to make regulations for the peace and good government of a scheduled area?
questions.e: The Governor may make regulations for the peace and good government of a scheduled area after consulting the Tribes Advisory Council. Such regulations require the assent of the President to take effect.

questions.q: The National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC) was originally set up as a statutory body in which year?
questions.e: Following the Mandal case judgment, the NCBC was established as a permanent statutory body in 1993. It was later granted constitutional status in 2018.

questions.q: Which of the following Union Territories does not have its own local legislature?
questions.e: Out of the UTs listed, Delhi, Puducherry, and Jammu and Kashmir have their own legislative assemblies. Ladakh is a union territory without a legislature.

questions.q: The total strength of the Legislative Assembly of Delhi is fixed at:
questions.e: The legislative assembly of the National Capital Territory of Delhi consists of 70 members who are directly elected by the people.

questions.q: Who determines the conditions of service of the chairman and members of a Joint State Public Service Commission (JSPSC)?
o: The Governors of the concerned states
questions.e: The number of members of a JSPSC and their conditions of service are determined by the President of India.

questions.q: Which of the following is the common High Court for Punjab, Haryana, and Chandigarh?
questions.e: Chandigarh is placed under the jurisdiction of the Punjab and Haryana High Court.

questions.q: The 69th Constitutional Amendment Act of 1991 granted a special status to which Union Territory?
questions.e: The 69th Amendment Act of 1991 provided a special status to the UT of Delhi and redesignated it as the National Capital Territory of Delhi.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding the Chairperson of the GST Council: 1️⃣ The Union Finance Minister is the Chairperson. 2️⃣ The Union Revenue Secretary is the Chairperson. 3️⃣ The Vice-Chairperson is chosen from amongst the members of the Council from the states.
questions.e: The Union Finance Minister serves as the Chairperson of the GST Council. The Vice-Chairperson is elected by the state members from among themselves.

questions.q: Which article of the Constitution deals with the "Administration of Scheduled Areas and Tribal Areas"?
questions.e: Article 244, located in Part X of the Constitution, envisages a special system of administration for areas designated as 'scheduled areas' and 'tribal areas'.

questions.q: The "watchdog of the merit system" in a state is:
questions.e: The Constitution visualizes the State Public Service Commission (SPSC) to be the 'watchdog of merit system' in the state.

questions.q: How many members of the UPSC should be persons who have held office for at least ten years under the Government?
questions.e: The Constitution requires that one-half of the members of the UPSC should be persons who have held office for at least ten years either under the Government of India or a state government.

questions.q: The Governor of which state is concurrently the Administrator of Chandigarh?
questions.e: According to the administrative arrangements, the Governor of Punjab serves concurrently as the Administrator of the Union Territory of Chandigarh.

questions.q: With reference to the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes (NCST), consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It was created by the 89th Constitutional Amendment Act. 2️⃣ It consists of a chairperson, a vice-chairperson and three other members. 3️⃣ The members hold office for a term of five years.
questions.e: The NCST was established by the 89th Amendment Act of 2003. It has five members (Chair, Vice-Chair, and three others). However, they hold office for a term of three years, not five.

questions.q: The jurisdiction of a state High Court can be extended to a Union Territory by:
questions.e: The Parliament has the power to establish a high court for a union territory or place a UT under the jurisdiction of the high court of an adjacent state.

questions.q: Which article provides for "Creation of local Legislatures or Council of Ministers or both for certain Union territories"?
questions.e: Article 239A of the Constitution deals with the creation of local legislatures or councils of ministers for specific union territories.

questions.q: The first commission to report on the administration of scheduled areas was headed by:
questions.e: The first commission for scheduled areas was appointed in 1960 and headed by U.N. Dhebar; it submitted its report in 1961.

questions.q: In the GST Council, a decision is taken by a majority of not less than:
questions.e: Every decision of the GST Council must be taken by a majority of at least three-fourths of the weighted votes of the members present and voting.

questions.q: Which of the following Union Territories were merged in 2020?
o: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
questions.e: In 2020, the separate union territories of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu were merged into a single union territory.

questions.q: Who is empowered to increase or decrease the area of an autonomous district under the Sixth Schedule?
questions.e: The Governor has the power to organize and re-organize autonomous districts, including increasing or decreasing their areas or changing their names.

questions.q: Which article of the Constitution deals with "Special provisions with respect to Delhi"?
questions.e: Article 239AA provides the specific legal and administrative framework for the National Capital Territory of Delhi.

questions.q: The chairman of the UPSC is appointed by:
questions.e: The Chairman and other members of the Union Public Service Commission are appointed by the President of India.

questions.q: Which of the following is not a member of the GST Council?
o: Union Minister of State in-charge of Revenue
questions.e: The GST Council includes the Union Finance Minister, the Union Minister of State for Finance/Revenue, and ministers nominated by each state government. Governors are not members.

questions.q: The Sixth Schedule applies to tribal areas in which of the following states?
questions.e: The Sixth Schedule specifically covers tribal areas in the four northeastern states of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram.

questions.q: Who determines the strength of a State Public Service Commission (SPSC)?
questions.e: The Constitution does not specify the strength of an SPSC but leaves it to the discretion of the Governor.

questions.q: The National Commission for Scheduled Castes (NCSC) must submit its annual report to:
questions.e: The NCSC presents an annual report to the President, who then places it before the Parliament.

questions.q: Which body was replaced by the National Commission for SCs and STs in 1990?
questions.e: The 65th Amendment Act of 1990 established the multi-member National Commission for SCs and STs, replacing the single Special Officer (Commissioner for SCs and STs).

questions.q: The Finance Commission is described as the "balancing wheel of fiscal federalism" in India. This role was traditionally undermined by:
questions.e: Until 2014, the role of the Finance Commission was often undermined by the non-constitutional Planning Commission in federal fiscal transfers.

questions.q: In the context of Union Territories, the administrator is an agent of the:
questions.e: An administrator of a union territory is an agent of the President and not a head of state like a governor.

questions.q: Which article empowers the President to make regulations for the peace, progress, and good government of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands?
questions.e: Article 240 gives the President power to make regulations for certain UTs, including the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Lakshadweep, and Ladakh.

questions.q: The Chairman of the NCSC holds office for a term of:
questions.e: According to the rules made by the President, the chairperson of the NCSC holds office for a term of three years.

questions.q: Which of the following UTs has its own High Court?
questions.e: Delhi is the only union territory that has a high court of its own, established in 1966.

questions.q: Who can remove the Chairman or a member of a State Public Service Commission?
questions.e: Although appointed by the Governor, the chairman and members of an SPSC can be removed only by the President.

questions.q: The National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC) was granted constitutional status by which amendment?
questions.e: The 102nd Amendment Act of 2018 conferred constitutional status on the NCBC by inserting Article 338-B.

questions.q: How many members of an autonomous district council under the Sixth Schedule are elected?
questions.e: A district council consists of 30 members, of whom 26 are elected on the basis of adult franchise.

questions.q: The legislative assembly of Puducherry can make laws on which subjects?
questions.e: The legislative assembly of Puducherry has the power to make laws on any subject of the State List and the Concurrent List.

questions.q: Who appoints the members of the Finance Commission?
questions.e: The Finance Commission consists of a chairman and four other members who are all appointed by the President.

questions.q: Which article of the Constitution deals with "Provision in case of failure of constitutional machinery" in Delhi?
questions.e: Article 239AB provides for the administration of Delhi in case of a failure of constitutional machinery, similar to Article 356 for states.

questions.q: The Sixth Schedule mentions how many tribal areas in the state of Meghalaya?
questions.e: There are three tribal areas in Meghalaya: Khasi Hills District, Jaintia Hills District, and Garo Hills District.

questions.q: In the GST Council, the votes of all the state governments combined have a weightage of:
questions.e: The combined votes of all state governments in a GST Council meeting have a weightage of two-thirds of the total votes cast.

questions.q: Who is empowered to declare an area as a 'scheduled area'?
questions.e: The President is empowered to declare an area to be a scheduled area and can also alter its boundaries.

questions.q: Which article of the Constitution deals with "Public Service Commissions for the Union and for the states"?
questions.e: Article 315 provides for the establishment of Public Service Commissions for the Union (UPSC) and for each of the states (SPSC).

questions.q: The Commissioner for SCs and STs was originally a:
questions.e: Originally, Article 338 provided for a single Special Officer, designated as the Commissioner for SCs and STs, to investigate safeguards.

questions.q: Which of the following is not a criteria for declaring an area as a 'scheduled area'? Preponderance of tribal population. Economic backwardness of the area.
o: Viable administrative entity like a District or Block.
questions.e: The established criteria include tribal population, compactness, administrative viability, and economic backwardness. Proximity to the capital is not a factor.

questions.q: The 7th Constitutional Amendment Act (1956) constituted which of the following?
questions.e: In 1956, the 7th Constitutional Amendment Act and the States Reorganisation Act constituted the 'union territories'.

questions.q: Who appoints the Chief Minister of Delhi?
questions.e: The Chief Minister of Delhi is appointed by the President, not by the Lieutenant Governor.

questions.q: The members of the National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC) hold office for a term of:
questions.e: Under the rules made by the President, the members of the NCBC hold office for a term of three years.

questions.q: Which High Court has jurisdiction over the Union Territory of Puducherry?
questions.e: The Union Territory of Puducherry is placed under the jurisdiction of the Madras High Court.

questions.q: The President can refer a matter to which court for an enquiry regarding the misbehaviour of a UPSC member?
questions.e: For cases of misbehaviour, the President must refer the matter to the Supreme Court for an enquiry.

questions.q: Which of the following states does not have tribal areas mentioned under the Sixth Schedule?
questions.e: The Sixth Schedule specifically covers tribal areas in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram. Nagaland is not included.

questions.q: In which year did the separate National Commission for Scheduled Castes come into existence?
questions.e: The separate National Commission for SCs came into existence in 2004 following the 89th Amendment Act.

questions.q: Who is the chairperson of the Home Minister's Advisory Committee (HMAC) for UTs?
questions.e: The HMAC is chaired by the Union Home Minister.

questions.q: Which article deals with "Appointment and term of office of members" of Public Service Commissions?
questions.e: Article 316 of the Constitution deals with the appointment and the term of office for members of both the UPSC and SPSCs.

questions.q: The "Mandal case" (1992) is also known as:
questions.e: The Mandal case judgment is officially known as Indra Sawhney vs. Union of India (1992).

questions.q: How many Finance Commissions have been constituted so far, as per the text?
questions.e: According to the provided text, fifteen Finance Commissions have been constituted till now.

questions.q: The 105th Amendment Act of 2021 is related to:
questions.e: The 105th Amendment Act of 2021 exempted state governments from consulting the NCBC for their own lists of backward classes.

questions.q: Which Union Territory was redesignated as the National Capital Territory of Delhi?
questions.e: The 69th Amendment Act of 1991 redesignated the Union Territory of Delhi as the National Capital Territory of Delhi.

questions.q: The salaries and allowances of SPSC members are charged on:
questions.e: The entire expenses of an SPSC are charged on the consolidated fund of the state and are not subject to a vote by the state legislature.

questions.q: Who can appoint the governor of a state as the administrator of an adjoining union territory?
questions.e: The President can appoint the governor of a state to act as the administrator of an adjacent union territory.

questions.q: The National Commission for STs presents its annual report to:
questions.e: The NCST presents an annual report to the President, who then lays it before the Parliament.

questions.q: Which article of the Constitution deals with the "Finance Commission"?
questions.e: Article 280 of the Constitution provides for the establishment of a Finance Commission.

questions.q: In the National Capital Territory of Delhi, the chief minister is appointed by:
questions.e: The chief minister of Delhi is appointed by the President of India.

questions.q: Which of the following is not a function of the Election Commission? Elections to Parliament. Elections to State Legislatures.
o: Elections to the office of President.
questions.e: The Election Commission is not concerned with elections to panchayats and municipalities, which are handled by State Election Commissions.

questions.q: The term of office for a member of the UPSC is:
o: Six years or 62 years of age
Five years or 65 years of age
Six years or 65 years of age
Five years or 62 years of age
questions.e: The chairman and members of the UPSC hold office for a term of six years or until they attain the age of 65 years.

questions.q: Which Constitutional Amendment Act provided for a separate National Commission for STs?
questions.e: The 89th Constitutional Amendment Act of 2003 bifurcated the combined commission into separate bodies for SCs and STs.

questions.q: In the GST Council, the vote of the central government has a weightage of:
questions.e: The vote of the central government in a GST Council meeting has a weightage of one-third of the total votes cast.

questions.q: Who is the nodal ministry for all matters of Union Territories?
questions.e: The Ministry of Home Affairs is the nodal ministry for all matters of Union Territories relating to legislation, finance, and services.

questions.q: Which article deals with "High Courts for Union territories"?
questions.e: Article 241 of the Constitution provides for the establishment of High Courts for union territories.

questions.q: The Chairman of the 15th Finance Commission is:
questions.e: According to Table 46.1, N.K. Singh is the Chairman of the 15th Finance Commission.

questions.q: Which of the following UTs was created in 2019?
questions.e: The Union Territory of Ladakh was created in 2019 following the bifurcation of the state of Jammu and Kashmir.

questions.q: The National Commission for Backward Classes consists of how many members in total?
questions.e: The NCBC consists of a chairperson, a vice-chairperson, and three other members, making a total of five members.

questions.q: Who is empowered to promulgate ordinances during the recess of the assembly in Delhi?
questions.e: The Lieutenant Governor of Delhi is empowered to promulgate ordinances during the recess of the legislative assembly.

questions.q: The "watchdog of the merit system" in India is:
questions.e: The Constitution visualizes the UPSC as the 'watchdog of merit system' in India.

questions.q: Which High Court has jurisdiction over the Union Territory of Chandigarh?
questions.e: Chandigarh is placed under the jurisdiction of the Punjab and Haryana High Court.

questions.q: The National Commission for SCs evaluates the progress of development of SCs under:
questions.e: The NCSC is tasked with advising on and evaluating the socio-economic development of SCs under both the Union and the states.

questions.q: Which of the following states has tribal areas mentioned in Table 42.1?
questions.e: Table 42.1 lists tribal areas in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram.

questions.q: The term of office for a member of an SPSC is:
o: Six years or 65 years of age
Six years or 62 years of age
Six years or 60 years of age
Five years or 62 years of age
questions.e: The chairman and members of a State Public Service Commission hold office for a term of six years or until they attain the age of 62 years.

questions.q: Who is the chairperson of the GST Council?
questions.e: The Union Finance Minister serves as the Chairperson of the GST Council.

questions.q: Which article deals with the "Creation of local Legislatures... for certain Union territories"?
questions.e: Article 239A provides for the creation of local legislatures or councils of ministers for certain union territories.

questions.q: The 69th Constitutional Amendment Act provided a special status to:
questions.e: The 69th Amendment Act of 1991 provided a special status to the Union Territory of Delhi.

questions.q: How many members are nominated to a Sixth Schedule district council?
questions.e: In a Sixth Schedule district council, four members are nominated by the Governor.

questions.q: Which High Court has jurisdiction over Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu?
questions.e: The Bombay High Court has jurisdiction over the union territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu.

questions.q: The Chairman of the Finance Commission should be a person having experience in:
questions.e: The chairman of the Finance Commission should be a person having experience in public affairs.

questions.q: Which article deals with "Special provisions with respect to Delhi"?
questions.e: Article 239AA contains the special provisions related to the National Capital Territory of Delhi.

questions.q: The separate National Commission for STs came into existence in:
questions.e: The separate National Commission for STs formally came into existence in 2004.

questions.q: Who determines the qualifications of members of the Finance Commission?
questions.e: The Constitution authorizes the Parliament to determine the qualifications of members of the Finance Commission.

questions.q: Which article of the Constitution deals with the "Administration of Union territories"?
questions.e: Article 239 of the Indian Constitution provides the general framework for the administration of Union Territories.

questions.q: The strength of the Legislative Assembly of Puducherry is:
questions.e: The legislative assembly of Puducherry consists of 30 members.

questions.q: Who is the chairperson of the Administrator's Advisory Committee (AAC) in a UT?
questions.e: The AAC is chaired by the Administrator of the concerned Union Territory.

questions.q: Which High Court has jurisdiction over the Union Territory of Andaman and Nicobar Islands?
questions.e: The Andaman and Nicobar Islands are under the jurisdiction of the Calcutta High Court.

questions.q: Which constitutional amendment conferred constitutional status on the NCBC?
questions.e: The 102nd Amendment Act of 2018 conferred constitutional status on the National Commission for Backward Classes.

questions.q: In the GST Council, what is the weightage of the combined votes of state governments?
questions.e: The votes of all state governments combined have a weightage of two-thirds in the GST Council.

questions.q: Who appoints the chairman and members of the UPSC?
questions.e: The chairman and members of the UPSC are appointed by the President.

questions.q: Which article deals with "Prohibition as to the holding of office by members of commission on ceasing to be such members"?
questions.e: Article 319 of the Constitution prohibits members of Public Service Commissions from holding certain offices after they cease to be members.

questions.q: The Sixth Schedule deals with the administration of tribal areas in how many northeastern states?
questions.e: The Sixth Schedule covers tribal areas in four states: Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram.

questions.q: Which article of the Constitution provides for a Finance Commission?
questions.e: Article 280 of the Indian Constitution provides for a Finance Commission as a quasi-judicial body.

questions.q: The separate National Commission for SCs consists of how many members in total?
questions.e: The separate NCSC consists of a chairperson, a vice-chairperson, and three other members, totaling five.

questions.q: Who is the chairperson of the Home Minister's Advisory Committee (HMAC)?
questions.e: The HMAC is chaired by the Union Home Minister.

questions.q: Which High Court has jurisdiction over the Union Territory of Lakshadweep?
questions.e: Lakshadweep is under the jurisdiction of the Kerala High Court.

questions.q: Which constitutional amendment bifurcated the combined commission for SCs and STs?
questions.e: The 89th Amendment Act of 2003 split the combined commission into two separate bodies for SCs and STs.

questions.q: Who is the chairperson of the GST Council?
questions.e: The Union Finance Minister serves as the Chairperson of the GST Council.

questions.q: Which article deals with "Special provisions with respect to Delhi"?
questions.e: Article 239AA provides special provisions for the National Capital Territory of Delhi.

questions.q: The Chairman and members of the Finance Commission hold office for:
o: Such period as specified by the President in his order
questions.e: Members of the Finance Commission hold office for the period specified by the President in the appointment order.

questions.q: Which High Court has jurisdiction over the Union Territory of Puducherry?
questions.e: Puducherry is under the jurisdiction of the Madras High Court.

questions.q: The National Commission for Backward Classes became a constitutional body through which amendment?
questions.e: The 102nd Amendment Act of 2018 granted constitutional status to the NCBC.

questions.q: Who appoints the chief minister of the National Capital Territory of Delhi?
questions.e: The chief minister of Delhi is appointed by the President.

questions.e: The SPSC is visualized as the 'watchdog of merit system' in the state.

questions.e: Article 244 in Part X of the Constitution deals with the administration of Scheduled Areas and Tribal Areas.

questions.q: The separate National Commission for STs consists of how many members in total?
questions.e: The separate NCST consists of a chairperson, a vice-chairperson, and three other members.

questions.q: Who is the ex-officio Secretary to the GST Council?
questions.e: The Union Revenue Secretary acts as the ex-officio Secretary to the GST Council.

questions.q: Which High Court has jurisdiction over the Union Territory of Andaman and Nicobar Islands?
questions.e: Andaman and Nicobar Islands are under the jurisdiction of the Calcutta High Court.

o: Delivering free, fair and transparent elections.
Enhancing active engagement. Deepening electoral democracy globally. Deepening electoral democracy in India.

questions.q: Which constitutional amendment redesignated Delhi as NCT?
questions.e: The 69th Amendment Act of 1991 redesignated Delhi as the National Capital Territory of Delhi.

questions.q: Who determines the strength of the Union Public Service Commission?
questions.e: The Constitution leaves the strength of the UPSC to the discretion of the President.

questions.q: Which article deals with "Functions of Public Service Commissions"?
questions.e: Article 320 of the Constitution defines the functions of the Public Service Commissions.

questions.q: The separate National Commission for SCs came into existence in:
questions.e: The separate NCSC formally came into existence in 2004.

questions.q: Which article deals with "Special provisions with respect to Delhi"?
questions.e: Article 239AA contains special provisions for Delhi.

questions.q: How many Finance Commissions have been constituted so far?
questions.e: Fifteen Finance Commissions have been constituted so far.

questions.q: Who appoints the chairperson of the National Commission for SCs?
questions.e: The chairperson of the NCSC is appointed by the President by warrant under his hand and seal.

questions.q: Which article deals with "Power of President to make regulations for certain Union territories"?

questions.q: The legislative assembly of Delhi consists of:
questions.e: The Delhi legislative assembly has 70 members.

questions.e: The Bombay High Court has jurisdiction over this UT.

questions.e: Article 239AB deals with the failure of constitutional machinery in Delhi.

questions.e: The Union Revenue Secretary is the ex-officio Secretary to the GST Council.

questions.e: Lakshadweep is under the jurisdiction of the Kerala High Court.

questions.q: The "Vision" of the Election Commission includes:
